text: nous thromboembolism has been noted in some studies.27 Statins also appear to have anti-inflammatory and immunomod- ulatory actions and these may contribute to their beneficial ef- fects. There is evidence from epidemiological studies that they reduce the risk of bacterial infections, although this has been at- tributed to a ‘healthy-user’ effect,28,29 and they may also reduce mortality in patients with sepsis.29 Benefit has also been reported in rheumatoid arthritis and other inflammatory arthropa- thies.30-33 In patients with organ transplantation, both cardiovas- cular and immunomodulatory actions may be of benefit (see below). However, the use of statins in these diseases remains to be confirmed.
